**Step 1 — Scene:** Three rectangular pieces of cheese pizza or pizza-style flatbread, with a mixed Greek-style salad.

**Step 2 — Vessel:** A large rounded-square dinner plate, approximately 27 cm across. Using a 27 cm circular approximation gives an area of **3.14 × 13.5² ≈ 572 cm²**.

**Step 3 — Items:** Cheese-and-tomato pizza; leafy greens; cucumber, tomato, red onion and pepper; dark olives; small feta crumbles; and a light visible dressing/oil sheen.

**Steps 4–7 — Area, volume, weight and energy:**

| Item | Plate area | Area × height = gross volume | Bulk density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Cheese pizza, including crust and sauce | 34% | 194 × 1.2 = 233 ml | 0.90 | 210 g | 270 | 567 kcal |
| Leafy greens | 19% | 109 × 3 = 327 ml | 0.15 | 49 g | 20 | 10 kcal |
| Cucumber, tomato, onion and pepper | 20% | 114 × 1.8 = 205 ml | 0.60 | 123 g | 25 | 31 kcal |
| Dark olives | 3% | 17 × 1.5 = 26 ml | 0.65 | 17 g | 145 | 25 kcal |
| Feta crumbles | 1% | 5.7 × 1.2 = 6.8 ml | 1.00 | 7 g | 265 | 19 kcal |
| Oil-based dressing | Overlay* | Approximately 6 ml | 1.00 | 6 g | 880 | 53 kcal |

The food footprints total **77% of the plate**. *Dressing coats the other foods, so it adds no separate footprint.*

**Step 8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **412 g and 705 kcal** is plausible for three modest pizza pieces and a substantial but loosely piled salad. The main uncertainties are crust thickness and dressing quantity.
